text: Then there is Lamine Yamal. A defense already has a problem on Barcelona's right: give him a one-on-one and he can beat his man; send help and the rest of the pitch changes shape. Sevilla shows the second consequence. For Raphinha's header, Yamal collects the ball and lifts it into the area. Raphinha attacks the delivery like a striker. Later, Rodri finds Yamal's run. Yamal slips the pass through, and Raphinha clips his finish over the keeper. Two different assists, two different finishes, and neither requires Yamal to score himself. This is the trap for a European back line. You can spend the evening preparing for Lamine's dribble, only to discover that your center backs are now dealing with Raphinha arriving on their blind side. Double one threat, and the other can become cleaner. Their partnership is not one rehearsed trick. The cross asks for a different defensive response from the through ball, and the speed of the next decision leaves little time to switch from one answer to the other.
